_about: How names and recurring terms are written in this language. Every translation follows this file, so a name is always spelled the same way. Names are written by sound, never translated (the author's rule). The spellings here are first versions based on the written names: the author's own pronunciation is recorded in Legacy/Behind The Scenes/World Lore/Word Pronunciation/Unique Words Pronounciation.wav, so correct any spelling here and later translations will follow it. Add new names the first time they are translated.
rule: Story names stay exactly as in English, as in Portuguese, Spanish, Malay, German and Vietnamese. That includes coined world terms written as names: creatures, plants, items, nari gels, spells, factions, guilds, places, ranks and coins (Wood People, Sand Worms, Fost Stone, Nari Refresher, Red Winga, Sapphire, Pearl). Plain words around them are translated into Italian and follow Italian word order (gel nari, pietre nari, bombe nari, interfaccia Darfaries, avventuriero Sapphire). Kingdoms read 'Regno di Sanbi', guards 'guardie di Forway'. The currency balls is 'palle' (singular 'palla'), which keeps the double meaning exactly; the rank follows it (palla sapphire, palle pearl). The unit timehunk stays as is. The reader is addressed as 'tu' everywhere, matching the author's casual voice; profanity is kept. Dates put the day first: '994 A.G. Adrian 6th' becomes '6 Adrian 994 A.G.' (the 1st is '1º'); with a weekday, 'Gannday, 14 Paulin 1039 A.G.'. Gregorian dates read '1º giugno 2020'. Category labels that are shared between pages use forms that fit any gender: Amichevoli, Ostili, Sulla difensiva. 'Sanbi shit!' (the Sanbi oath) is always 'Vecchia anima di Sanbi!' ('Old Sanbi soul!'), the author's rule; 'Sanbi shit out of luck' becomes 'Ti resterà solo la sfiga, vecchia anima di Sanbi!'. Standard Italian spelling.
